chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forsakes his wife without divorce or an oath, for a year, not approaching her bed. He said: 'Let him go to his family.'
He said: 'Any man who makes an oath of al-ila' from his wife, and al-ila' is that the man says:
By Allah, I will not have intercourse with you for such and such [period], or he says:
Then she waits for him for four months, and after the four months he is taken and brought to a standstill (to be given a choice).
If he returns (to the marriage), and al-ifa' is that he reconciles with his family, then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
If he does not return, he is compelled to divorce, and a divorce does not take effect between them until he is brought to a standstill.
And it is also after the four months that he is compelled to either return (to the marriage) or divorce.

key_terms.اَلْإِيفَاءُ: Reconciliation or fulfilling the oath by resuming relations
key_terms.اَلْإِيلاَءُ: Oath of abstention from sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of al-ila' (oath of abstention) and how long does the wife wait?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between simple estrangement (*hijr*) and the formal oath of abstention (*ila'*), establishing the four-month waiting period derived from the Quran. It emphasizes that upon the expiration of this period, the husband is judicially compelled to either reconcile (*ifa'*) or effect a divorce, preventing indefinite limbo in the marital bond. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on resolving marital uncertainty through clear legal mechanisms rather than prolonged silence.
